original_question: If mu is a continuous even convex function on [-1, 1] with mu >= 0, does the associated snake polynomial always have a nonnegative expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Conjecture 7.1 (Geno Nikolov), rather than the broader Problem 7.1: for continuous even convex majorants mu >= 0 on [-1,1], the snake polynomials associated with mu are conjectured to have non-negative expansions in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of Conjecture 7.1 in Section 7: the hypotheses on mu (continuous, even, convex, nonnegative on [-1,1]) and the intended conclusion about nonnegative expansion in the first-kind Chebyshev basis are exactly the paper's target.
missing_details: The paper is speaking about the family of n-th snake polynomials associated with mu, so the degree parameter n must be quantified explicitly.
The ambient polynomial space should be stated: P_n is the space of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n.

To make the question stand-alone, the n-th snake polynomial must be defined via its extremal/alternation property: |omega_mu(x)| <= mu(x) on [-1,1] and omega_mu(tau_i^*) = (-1)^i mu(tau_i^*) at n+1 ordered alternation points.
Because the snake polynomial is unique only up to orientation, the sign convention must be fixed; otherwise the phrase 'nonnegative expansion' is ambiguous.

The existence clause used in Section 7 is implicit in the draft: one assumes there exists a nonzero P in P_n with -mu(x) <= P(x) <= mu(x) on [-1,1], so that the corresponding n-th snake polynomial is defined.
The conclusion should spell out what 'nonnegative expansion' means: omega_mu(x) = sum_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with a_j >= 0 for all j.
The draft says 'the associated snake polynomial' in the singular, but the paper's conjecture concerns all associated snake polynomials, i.e. all degrees n for which they are defined.
refined_question: For every n in N, let P_n be the real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n, and let mu in C[-1,1] satisfy mu(x) >= 0, mu(-x) = mu(x), and convexity on [-1,1]. Assume there exists a nonzero polynomial P in P_n such that -mu(x) <= P(x) <= mu(x) for all x in [-1,1], and let omega_{mu,n} in P_n denote the n-th snake polynomial associated with mu, normalized by the alternation condition omega_{mu,n}(tau_i^*) = (-1)^i mu(tau_i^*) at some points 1 >= tau_0^* > tau_1^* > ... > tau_n^* >= -1 and by |omega_{mu,n}(x)| <= mu(x) on [-1,1]. Must omega_{mu,n} always admit a first-kind Chebyshev expansion omega_{mu,n}(x) = sum_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with all coefficients a_j >= 0?
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Conjecture 7.1 in Section 7, not at the broader class-finding Problem 7.1. I therefore kept the scope exactly on the even-convex-majorant conjecture and only added the nearby Section 7 definitions needed to make it self-contained: the quantifier over n, the real polynomial space P_n, the alternation-point definition of the n-th snake polynomial, the existence condition under the majorant, and the orientation normalization needed for 'nonnegative coefficients' to be meaningful. I did not replace the question by the Markov/Duffin-Schaeffer extremality statement, because Theorem 7.3 gives motivation for the conjecture but not an equivalence.
